_about: Skill choreography commands (script.dat events 15xxxxxx / 12000xxx). sure: verified = tested in game, high = clear from the handler or the data, guess = from how vanilla skills use it. Positions are in 1/10 'dots' relative to an actor; actor 1256 = the caster, 1254/1255 = other battle actors, 300-399 = locator actors made with cmd_66b0. Times are frames (60 per second). 'traced' = read from the command's code in disgaea5.exe and checked against recordings of the game (2026-10-10).

wait.desc: pause this event for N frames

wait_children.desc: wait until every event started by this one has finished, then END this event (anything after it never runs)

wait_children_c.desc: wait until every event started by this one has finished, then go on

call_event.desc: run another event (and its arguments). 12000010 / 12000011 = skill start / end, 12000020 = actor motion sequence, 12000045 = damage hits at the listed frames, 12000055 / 12000056 = camera to caster / back

spawn_event.desc: start another event in parallel (no wait)

se_play.desc: play sound effect (SE id, volume 0-240, pitch / speed 1000 = normal?)

voice_play_actor.desc: play a voice line of the caster

cmd_3c00.desc: load effect model effectNNNN.obf (Effect.dat) into effect slot 0-255. Swap the number to change what is drawn

cmd_3c02.desc: remove the effect in the slot

cmd_3c10.desc: show the slot's effect at an actor + offset (offsets turn with the skill's facing); size 1000 = 100% (the same value cmd_3c40 changes); step = model frames per game frame x 1000 (1000 normal, 2000 double, 0 = hold the frame); plays = how many times its animation runs before it disappears (0 / 1 once, -1 forever)

cmd_3c18.desc: show the slot's effect like cmd_3c10, playing the model's animation from frame 'from' (to 'to'; 0 = its end)

cmd_3c20.desc: show the slot's effect attached to an actor (it follows the actor)

cmd_3c22.desc: show attached to an actor, from frame 'from'

cmd_3c30.desc: which picture layer of a two-layer (LA88) texture the effect uses (0 sharp, 1 the softened copy)

cmd_3c40.desc: size of the effect in percent per axis over N frames (replaces the show's size; 0 hides it)

cmd_3c42.desc: size per axis over N frames, eased

cmd_3c44.desc: set / scale size (percent) over N frames

cmd_3c64.desc: turn the effect TO rx / ry / rz degrees over N frames (roll, then pitch, then yaw)

cmd_3c68.desc: turn the effect BY rx / ry / rz degrees over N frames

cmd_3c74.desc: second rotation of the effect: BY degrees (it does not move the effect)

cmd_3c80.desc: colour and opacity in percent over N frames (100 = as drawn; above 100 does not brighten)

cmd_3ca0.desc: draw the effect nearer the camera by value / 20 map units (100 = 5): it then sits on the ground or a unit without cutting into it, and comes later in the sorted draw queue (0x14017c790 -> 0x14030aba0 / 0x14030b4d0)

cmd_3cb8.desc: size of each piece of the model (percent) without moving the pieces apart -- e.g. small dots on a big ring

cmd_3cd6.desc: blending of every part of the effect (0x14017d020 → inst+0x1a0; the blend state 0x1403d6ba0): 1 normal, 2 adds light, 3 takes light away (screen − colour), 4 multiplies (see-through parts fade to white), 5 colour − screen; 255 = the model's own

cmd_3cda.desc: the effect's opacity to alpha % over N frames (the alpha byte of its colour; 3c80 sets the whole colour) (0x14017d170)

cmd_4428.desc: stop / fade the emitter after N frames

cmd_4480.desc: emit particles at an actor + offset

cmd_4490.desc: emit a particle stream at an actor + offset

cmd_44b5.desc: emit particles in a ring / sphere around an actor

cmd_4140.desc: move the effect to an actor + offset over N frames (straight)

cmd_4170.desc: fly the effect to an actor + offset over N frames, eased (projectiles)

cmd_3210.desc: camera: aim at an actor + offset over N frames (straight)

cmd_3220.desc: camera: aim at an actor + offset over N frames, eased (ease 200 = speeding up, -200 = slowing down; flag 1)

cmd_3230.desc: camera distance (zoom) over N frames: 700 = the battle view, smaller = closer; 0 = back to the default

cmd_3240.desc: camera distance (zoom) over N frames, eased (ease 200 = speeding up, -200 = slowing down; flag 1)

cmd_32a0.desc: camera shake for N frames: the camera jumps by the amounts / 100 map units (sideways along the view, up-down), alternating every 2 frames; frames -1 = until another shake (e.g. 0, 80, 6 = a hit)

screen_fade.desc: fade the screen over N frames: 127 = black, 129 (-127) = white, 0 = clear, 192 = half white

cmd_6510.desc: play a sprite motion on an actor: 0 idle, 100/101 attack, 109 cast, 151 cast release, the class's own special poses 7001...

cmd_6530.desc: jump the actor's motion to frame N (0x14016d070: the sprite's time = N); it does not wait — the script goes straight on

cmd_65a0.desc: scale an actor (percent) over N frames

cmd_65b4.desc: turn the actor's sprite BY degrees over N frames (clockwise in the sprite's own picture: mirrored sprites turn the other way), around a pivot (x 0.1875 sprite pixels)

cmd_65b8.desc: turn the actor's sprite TO an angle (the short way round) over N frames, around a pivot (x 0.1875 sprite pixels from its anchor, y down)

cmd_6642.desc: move an actor to another actor + offset over N frames (0 = at once): mode 0 straight, 1 / 2 / 5 / 6 an arc (the offset's height = the apex)

cmd_6672.desc: move an actor to another actor + offset over N frames: mode 0 speeds up / slows down step by step (ease 200 / -200), 100 eased, 1 / 2 / 5 / 6 / 11 / 12 / 21 / 22 arcs (the offset's height = the apex)

cmd_66b0.desc: create locator 300-399 at an actor + offset (a point other commands can use as 'actor')

cmd_6480.desc: tint an actor's sprite (percent) over N frames; alpha 0 hides it. Actor 10000 = every other unit on the map

cmd_6c04.desc: the actor moves with another one from now on (the Killia you see in Macrocosm follows the hidden caster)

cmd_72f0.desc: mirror the skill from now on (1) or not (0): sideways offsets, effect turns and sizes, camera aim and turns, actor moves and sprite turns flip -- skills use it for facings 1 and 2

cmd_7220.desc: deal this % of the skill's damage to the actor now (shows the number). A choreography that never calls it deals NO damage; several calls split it (shares should add up to 100). Targets: 3600 (single), 3000-3015 for area skills (present when $60400+i == 1)

cmd_7228.desc: finish the actor's damage (every vanilla damaging skill ends with it, 30 frames)

cmd_3250.desc: the camera's lens over N frames: field of view 27008 / lens degrees (vertical); 0 = the battle's 5120 (5.3°, narrow); smaller = wider (Macrocosm's planet: 700-1500)

cmd_325c.desc: the camera stops turning (its rotation keeps the current angle; aim and zoom go on; 0x140166fd0)

cmd_3260.desc: turn the camera BY pitch / yaw / roll degrees over N frames (minus turns the other way)

cmd_3268.desc: turn the camera TO an angle: pitch 30 - value, yaw = the battle view's yaw - value, roll -value (0,0,0,0 = the battle view)

cmd_3280.desc: turn the camera BY degrees over N frames, eased

cmd_3290.desc: turn the camera back to the battle view over N frames

cmd_2820.desc: colour and opacity of the battle map in percent over N frames (alpha 0 hides the map: the backdrop shows)

cmd_2830.desc: backdrop behind everything: 4 corner colours (top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right; 128 = full) over N frames

cmd_2832.desc: backdrop gradient over N frames: colour 1 to colour 2, top to bottom (vertical 1) or left to right (0); 128 = full

cmd_2834.desc: backdrop in one colour over N frames (128 = full)

cmd_2835.desc: backdrop back to the map's own colours over N frames

cmd_3c6a.desc: turn the effect BY degrees, eased

cmd_3c70.desc: second rotation of the effect (applied after the first): TO degrees

cmd_3c78.desc: rotation order of the effect (0-5 first rotation, 6-11 second)

cmd_3c90.desc: model frames per game frame x 990 (animation speed of the model)

cmd_3cbc.desc: the effect takes the size and turn of the actor it is attached to

cmd_3cbd.desc: the effect takes the turn of the actor it is attached to

cmd_3cbe.desc: the effect takes the size of the actor it is attached to

cmd_3cc6.desc: jump the model's animation to a frame

cmd_3cd8.desc: face the camera: 1 always, 2 turning only around the vertical, 0 never (-1 = the model's own)

cmd_3cdc.desc: opacity in percent over N frames, eased

cmd_6402.desc: give an extra actor the look of a class (its sprite): 20 = Killia's second form, 7000 / 7002 = event poses

cmd_640a.desc: switch the actor on; waits while its sprite files are still loading (0x1401689d0 rewinds the script and returns 0)

cmd_6411.desc: make the actor the cut-in portrait of another (its picture file 10000 + sprite, animations 8000-8100)

cmd_6460.desc: 1: the actor is drawn on the screen (cut-in), not in the world

cmd_6482.desc: opacity of an actor (percent) over N frames

cmd_6620.desc: the actor's base place = where it is now (plain references to it point there)

cmd_6680.desc: jump an actor to another actor + offset over N frames: the offset's height is how high it jumps (mode 2: lands at the destination's own height; 1 / 5: on the ground there; 6: see the docs); ease_up_down shapes the arc's timing, ease_sideways the sideways speed

cmd_6660.desc: place a screen actor (cut-in) at x / y tenths of a 1080p pixel from the screen centre

cmd_6664.desc: move a screen actor (cut-in) to x / y (tenths of a 1080p pixel from the centre) over N frames, eased

cmd_66b8.desc: move a locator by an offset

cmd_65b5.desc: turn the actor's sprite BY degrees, eased

cmd_65c1.desc: turn the actor's sprite TO an angle, eased

cmd_65bc.desc: draw the actor's sprite shifted by x / y (x 0.1875 sprite pixels, y down: 0, -300 lifts it)

cmd_32f8.desc: mirror the camera aim only (see cmd_72f0)

cmd_3cd4.desc: mirror effect shows and flights only (see cmd_72f0)

cmd_65f0.desc: mirror sprite turns / animations only (see cmd_72f0)

cmd_66f8.desc: mirror actor moves and points only (see cmd_72f0)

cmd_3cde.desc: draw queue of the whole effect (0-11, drawn in that order; 6 is sorted back to front with the units, 4 / 5 come before them = behind every unit); without it each part uses its mesh layer byte + 2 (0x14017d5e0)

cmd_3c9a.desc: 0: hide the effect (its animation stops too), 1: show it again (0x14017c6f0)

cmd_3ca5.desc: 1: the effect's camera-facing (billboard) parts stop facing the camera (0x14017c860)

cmd_3c98.desc: stores a value on the effect (+0x22a) that nothing reads (0x14017c640)

cmd_6610.desc: a unit value at +0x2c = value / 100 (negative: 0.163); not drawing (0x14016f820)

cmd_6560.desc: stop (0) or play at 100 % (anything else) the actor's motion (0x14016d530; the same speed as cmd_6570, an earlier speed is not kept)

cmd_6570.desc: the actor's motion speed in percent (0x14016d860)

cmd_6470.desc: the actor's shadow: 0 none, 1-4 how it finds the ground under it (0x14016a5b0 -> actor +0x25c, read by 0x140149bd7)

cmd_6410.desc: give the actor a look: source = mode x 10000 + number (u16): 0 / 1 like actor N, 2 a unit, 3 class N, 5 sprite N (9100 = an invisible helper); 0x140168d70

cmd_6630.desc: put the actor at a place at once (cmd_6642 with no offset and 0 frames; 0x14016fa00)
